R001.text: Fix a Euclidean space X, A⊆X and a real s; assume L1: s>0. Give X its Borel measurable structure. M001 with d=s identifies native μH[s](A) with the scale-cover formula. For positive s the empty-member summands vanish and each nonempty finite-diameter member has the ordinary real diameter power used in H. The supremum over extended positive scales equals the supremum over finite positive scales: the infimum at scale ∞ is no larger than the infimum at any finite scale. Countable covers are equivalent to sequences by enumeration and empty padding, with the same cost. Thus μH[s](A)=H^s(A). Restricting covers to smaller diameter bounds can only increase their infimum, so H^s_δ(A)≥H^s_r(A) whenever 0<δ≤r. The definition of H is its supremum over these contents; if that supremum is ∞, for every finite bound there is a scale exceeding the bound, and every smaller scale still exceeds it. Discharge L1 and universally generalize the arbitrary space, subset and exponent; F001 records this general statement with fresh bound names.

For the arbitrary X,A,s assume L6: s>0. Under the additional antecedent L7: s<dim_H(A), apply M002 with the nonnegative real u=s; F001 converts its conclusion to H^s(A)=∞, and discharging L7 proves that implication. Under L8: dim_H(A)<s, M003 similarly gives H^s(A)=0; discharge L8. Under L9: H^s(A)=0, F001 gives μH[s](A)=0≠∞, so M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s; discharge L9. Under L10: H^s(A)=∞, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A); discharge L10. Discharge L6 and universally quantify the arbitrary space, subset and exponent. Nonnegativity of dimension follows from its definition as a supremum in [0,∞].

For monotonicity fix B⊆X and temporarily assume L2: A⊆B. At every positive exponent s, any scale cover of B covers A, so its infimum bounds the content of A; taking suprema gives H^s(A)≤H^s(B). If dim_H(A)>dim_H(B), real order density supplies a finite positive exponent strictly between them (also when dim_H(A)=∞). F002 at that exponent and each set would give infinity on A and zero on B, contradicting the measure inequality. Hence dim_H(A)≤dim_H(B); discharge L2. For isometry let Y be Euclidean and assume L3: φ:A→Y preserves distances. Intersect the members of any cover of A with A and apply φ; they cover φ(A) with no greater diameters. Conversely inverse images in A of a cover of φ(A) cover A with no greater diameters, because φ preserves distance. Infima at each scale in both directions give equal contents at every positive exponent, and then H^s(φ(A))=H^s(A). If the dimensions differed, a positive finite exponent between them and F002 would again give zero on one side and infinity on the other. Discharge L3 and universally quantify X,A,B,Y,φ. The scale and critical assertions already hold universally by F001 and F002.

For arbitrary a>0, M012 at x=0 and q=a gives continuity of h↦h^a at zero, since 0≤a; its value is 0, so h^a→0 also through positive h. For arbitrary b<0, M013 gives h^b→∞ as h↓0. Finally the finite geometric identities Σ_{i=0}^{m-1}2^{-i-1}=1-2^{-m} and Σ_{i=0}^{m-1}2^{-i-2}=(1-2^{-m})/2 follow by telescoping the finite geometric sums. For m=0, 2^m≥m+1; the induction step follows from 2·(m+1)≥m+2 for m≥0. Thus 2^m≥m+1 for all natural m, so the remainders tend to zero by the Archimedean property, and taking suprema of the partial sums gives the two exported series values. Close the positive/negative exponent conditions as implications and quantify a,b.

R002.text: H003 and the open-cover definition of compactness give boundedness: the nested open balls about the origin with positive integer radii cover V(n), hence E; a finite subcover is contained in one such ball and therefore in [-R,R]^n for some real R≥1. For arbitrary s>0 and δ>0 (L1), the open balls of radius δ/2 centered at points of E cover E. H003 gives a finite subcover. Each ball has diameter at most δ by the triangle inequality, so its s-cost is finite, and the finite sum bounds H^s_δ(E). Discharge L1 and quantify s,δ.

Choose R from F001. If n>0 (L2), for 0<h≤1 and a>n (L3), divide each coordinate interval [-R,R] into ceil(2R/h) closed equal subintervals, each of length at most h. The resulting cubes cover E, number at most (2R+1)^n h^{-n}, and have diameters at most √n h: the sum of the n squared coordinate differences is at most n h². Thus their total a-cost is at most (2R+1)^n n^{a/2} h^{a-n}. By the positive-power limit in N001 this tends to zero as h↓0. For every fixed target scale and positive cost tolerance, take h small enough for both inequalities; H^a at each scale and then H^a(E) are zero. N001 gives D≤a for every a>n, hence D≤n by order density. Discharge L3,L2. If n=0 (L4), H002 and the empty-tuple definition of V(0) give E=V(0), a singleton. Its singleton cover has zero s-cost at every scale for every s>0; N001 gives D≤s for all s>0, hence D=0. Discharge L4. In both cases D≥0 by N001 and D≤n. Together with F002 this proves the dimension, boundedness and finite-content assertions.

Finally the concatenation map in V has inverse that deletes the last coordinate and records it separately. For arbitrary x,y∈V(n) and real t,u, the squared distance between the two concatenated tuples is Σ_{j<n}(x_j-y_j)^2+(t-u)^2, exactly the squared product distance. Taking nonnegative square roots proves isometry, and the displayed inverse proves bijectivity. Its restriction sends F exactly to the required E×[0,1] in V(n+1), with no change of norm.

R003.text: Assume L1: n≥1, q>D, 0<r≤1 and ε>0, with q,r,ε arbitrary. N002 gives D≥0, hence q>0. N001 gives H^q(E)=0 and therefore H^q_r(E)=0. By the defining infimum of H^q_r, there is a countable scale-r cover of E of q-cost <ε/2: if all admissible costs were at least ε/2 their infimum would be at least ε/2. Countable covers may be enumerated by ℕ and padded with empty members.

Choose W from F001. Discard empty members and let K={i:W_i≠∅}. A nonempty zero-diameter W_i is a singleton, since distance zero identifies any two of its points. For each such i take the positive number min(r/2,(ε2^{-i-3})^{1/q}) and replace W_i by the closed ball centered at its unique point, with radius half that number. It has positive diameter at most r and q-cost ≤ε2^{-i-3}<ε2^{-i-2}; the power identity is valid because q>0. The diameter is exactly the prescribed number because n≥1: two opposite points in the first-coordinate direction belong to the closed ball, and the triangle inequality supplies the reverse diameter bound. Leave every positive-diameter member unchanged. Define U_i to be this resulting family on K and r_i=diam(U_i). The cover still contains every W_i and hence covers E, with 0<r_i≤r. Its total q-cost is at most the original cost plus Σ_{i≥0}ε2^{-i-2}≤ original cost+ε/2<ε, using the geometric sum in N001 and finite-partial-sum comparisons. This is the supplied replacement argument with an explicit permissible choice of the small diameters. Discharge L1 and universally quantify q,r,ε.

R004.text: If n=0 (L1), N002 says that E is the singleton V(0) and D=0. For each positive integer m, divide I into m equal closed pieces and take their products with E. They cover F, each has Euclidean diameter 1/m, and their total a-cost for any a>1 is m^{1-a}=(1/m)^{a-1}→0 by N001. Diameters also tend to zero, so at each target scale the content is zero; hence H^a(F)=0. N001 gives dim_H(F)≤a for all a>1, whence dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L1.

Now assume L2: n≥1. Fix q>D and δ>0 (L3), and independently fix ε>0 (L4). Set r=min(1,δ/√2). By N002, q>0; N003 supplies a countable cover U on K with r_i=diam(U_i)∈(0,r] and Σ_i r_i^q<ε. Set N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Partition I into N_i closed intervals [j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i], 0≤j<N_i, of lengths 1/N_i≤r_i. Since r_i≤1, N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. The products U_i×[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i] cover F and form a countable family indexed by the countable union of finite index sets. For two points in one such product, the squared distance is at most r_i²+r_i²; hence its diameter is at most √2 r_i≤δ. Their total (q+1)-cost is bounded by Σ_i N_i(√2 r_i)^{q+1}≤2(√2)^{q+1}Σ_i r_i^q<2(√2)^{q+1}ε. All diameters and costs here are finite, and q+1>0.

Discharge L4 and universally quantify ε in F002. For the fixed q and δ the content is bounded by 2(√2)^{q+1}ε for every ε>0, so the nonnegative content H^{q+1}_δ(F) is zero. This is true for every δ>0, hence H^{q+1}(F)=0. N001 gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. N002 makes D finite, and this inequality for every q>D implies dim_H(F)≤D+1: a strictly larger dimension would admit a finite q>D with q+1 below it. Discharge L3 and L2. The natural-number cases n=0 and n≥1 are exhaustive; combining with F001 gives the asserted upper bound.

R005.text: The closed interval I=[0,1] is Borel measurable. M010 with a=0,b=1 gives λ(I)=max(1-0,0)=1.

Fix arbitrary B,ρ,η and assume L1: B≠∅, 0≤ρ<∞, diam(B)≤ρ and η>0. For any point of B all other points lie within ρ of it, so B is bounded above and below. Real completeness gives finite α=inf B and β=sup B, with α≤b≤β for every b∈B. For every b∈B the diameter bound implies every element of B is ≤b+ρ; thus β≤b+ρ. Consequently β-ρ is a lower bound of B, so β-ρ≤α and β-α≤ρ. Define J=(α-η/2,β+η/2). Positivity of η and α≤b≤β put B inside J; its length is β-α+η>0 and ≤ρ+η. An open interval and its intersection with the closed interval I are Borel measurable. M009 with endpoints α-η/2 and β+η/2 gives λ(J)=β-α+η. Measure monotonicity gives λ(J∩I)≤λ(J)≤ρ+η. Discharge L1 and quantify B,ρ,η. Together with F001 this proves every clause of the exported enclosure statement.

R006.text: Fix s,δ and assume L1: s>0,δ>0. Put c=H^s_δ(E), finite by N002. Let W be an arbitrary scale-δ cover of F (L2), indexed by ℕ with empty padding allowed. Put ρ_i=diam(W_i)≤δ and let A_i,B_i be its two coordinate projections. The squared Euclidean product-distance formula shows each projection decreases distance. Taking suprema of distances gives diam(A_i)≤ρ_i and diam(B_i)≤ρ_i. Empty members have empty projections and zero diameter; nonempty members have nonempty projections.

Fix ε>0 (L3) and define η_i=ε2^{-i-1}/(1+ρ_i^s)>0. For each nonempty W_i, apply N005 to B_i, the diameter bound ρ_i from F001 and η_i: define its explicit enclosing open interval J_i, of length and Lebesgue measure at most ρ_i+η_i. For empty W_i let J_i=∅. In all cases J_i and J_i∩I are Borel, B_i⊆J_i, and λ(J_i∩I)≤ρ_i+η_i. For each t∈I the A_i with t∈J_i cover E: given x∈E, (x,t)∈F lies in some W_i, so x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. By the content infimum and diam(A_i)≤ρ_i, c≤Σ_i ρ_i^s 1_{J_i}(t). This argument makes no measurability assertion about W_i,A_i or B_i.

Define f_i=ind(J_i∩I,ρ_i^s) on ℝ. Each is measurable: on the Borel set J_i∩I it is a constant and on its Borel complement it is zero; inverse images of Borel sets are therefore one of these sets, ∅, or ℝ. In particular it is λ-almost-everywhere measurable. F002 gives ind(I,c)≤Σ_i f_i pointwise on all ℝ, since outside I both sides vanish.

M008 applied to the pointwise inequality F003 gives the corresponding inequality of nonnegative integrals. M007 on I with c and N005's λ(I)=1 identifies the left integral with c. M006 exchanges the nonnegative sum and integral, using the measurability already proved in F003; M007 on each J_i∩I with coefficient ρ_i^s then gives c≤Σ_i ρ_i^s λ(J_i∩I). By F002 this is at most Σ_i ρ_i^{s+1}+Σ_i η_iρ_i^s≤Σ_i ρ_i^{s+1}+ε, since η_iρ_i^s=ε2^{-i-1}ρ_i^s/(1+ρ_i^s)≤ε2^{-i-1} and N001 gives Σ_i2^{-i-1}=1. The product and sum comparisons follow first for finite partial sums and then by their suprema; thus they remain valid if a series is infinite. This is Tonelli for nonnegative terms, without finite-integrability premises or an exchange of signed series.

Discharge L3 and quantify ε in F004: for every ε>0, c≤Σ_iρ_i^{s+1}+ε. If the series is infinite, c≤Σ_iρ_i^{s+1} is immediate. Otherwise it is a finite real, and order density applied to the inequality for every ε>0 gives c≤Σ_iρ_i^{s+1}. Since W was an arbitrary δ-cover, c is a lower bound of every admissible (s+1)-cost; therefore c≤H^{s+1}_δ(F), their infimum. Discharge L2, then L1, and universally quantify s,δ. This proves the asserted inequality with exactly the same scale on both sides.

R007.text: Assume L1: D>0. N002 gives finite D. Fix 0<s<D (L2). By N001, H^s(E)=∞, so H^s_δ(E) is unbounded as δ↓0. N006 gives H^s_δ(E)≤H^{s+1}_δ(F) for each δ>0. Taking suprema over δ proves H^{s+1}(F)=∞. N001 therefore gives dim_H(F)≥s+1.

Discharge L2 and quantify s: dim_H(F)≥s+1 for every 0<s<D. These s exist because D>0. Their supremum is D, by real order density. Hence dim_H(F)≥D+1. Discharge L1 to obtain exactly the exported conditional lower bound.

R008.text: For arbitrary a>1 (L1), partition I into m equal closed subintervals for every positive integer m. Diameters are 1/m and total a-cost is m^{1-a}=(1/m)^{a-1}→0 by N001. At any fixed positive target scale these covers eventually qualify and have arbitrarily small cost. Hence every scale content and H^a(I) are zero; N001 yields dim_H(I)≤a for all a>1, and thus dim_H(I)≤1. Discharge L1 and quantify a.

Fix 0<s<1 and δ>0 (L2), and any scale-δ cover W of I (L3), with ρ_i=diam(W_i)≤δ. For arbitrary ε>0 (L4), enclose each nonempty W_i in the open interval J_i provided by N005 with η=ε2^{-i-1}; take J_i=∅ for empty W_i. These intervals cover I and satisfy λ(J_i)≤ρ_i+ε2^{-i-1}. By N005, λ(I)=1; measure monotonicity and M011 applied to J give 1≤λ(⋃_iJ_i)≤Σ_iλ(J_i)≤Σ_iρ_i+ε, the last estimate using the geometric sum in N001 and finite-partial-sum comparisons. Let ε↓0: if Σ_iρ_i is infinite the conclusion is automatic, otherwise order density gives Σ_iρ_i≥1. Discharge L4. Arbitrary covering sets need not be measurable, since only the enclosing intervals have entered the length estimate.

For positive ρ_i≤δ and s<1, ρ_i^{s-1}≥δ^{s-1}, so ρ_i^s≥δ^{s-1}ρ_i. For ρ_i=0 the same inequality is 0≥0 because s>0. Summing finite partial sums and taking their suprema gives Σ_iρ_i^s≥δ^{s-1}Σ_iρ_i≥δ^{s-1} by F002. Since W was arbitrary, infimizing gives H^s_δ(I)≥δ^{s-1}. Discharge L3. N001 gives δ^{s-1}→∞ as δ↓0 because s-1<0; consequently H^s(I)=∞. N001 gives dim_H(I)≥s for every 0<s<1, so dim_H(I)≥1 by order density. Discharge L2 and quantify s,δ. With F001 this proves all clauses of the exported interval-dimension statement.

R009.text: N002 gives 0≤D≤n and finite D. If D>0 (L1), N007 gives dim_H(F)≥D+1; discharge L1. If D=0 (L2), choose x_0∈E by H002 and define φ:I→V(n)×ℝ by φ(t)=(x_0,t). The Euclidean product-distance formula gives d(φ(t),φ(u))=|t-u|, so φ is distance preserving and φ(I)⊆F. N001 gives dim_H(φ(I))=dim_H(I) and monotonicity gives dim_H(F)≥dim_H(φ(I)). N008 states dim_H(I)=1, hence dim_H(F)≥1=D+1 in this branch, including n=0. Discharge L2. Nonnegativity makes these cases exhaustive. N004 supplies the opposite bound, giving dim_H(F)=D+1. Finally N002's bijective concatenation isometry identifies this exact metric and set with E×[0,1]⊆ℝ^{n+1}; by N001 the dimension is unchanged. Substitution of D=dim_H(E) proves the full target.

1: # Shared-lemma extraction as a local NL0 revision
2: 
3: ## Scope and position
4: 
5: Apply this procedure at the start of **NL0-to-Lean translation**, before final
6: interface/planning freeze or worker-packet generation. It is not an extra
7: requirement for a task that requests NL0 alone. The input is an existing,
8: versioned NL0, not an invitation to reconstruct its proof.
9: 
10: The operation is proof factoring: move an already supplied local derivation
11: into one shared N/R pair and replace its occurrences by explicit applications.
12: Do not rewrite the whole NL0, regenerate its prose, reprove unchanged results,
13: or seek a stronger/general theorem for speculative future reuse. Reading the
14: existing graph to locate candidates is not a new proof-construction task.
15: If an existing N already exports the needed fact, reuse that node directly.
16: 
17: Use [the revision record](../templates/source-refactoring.md). Preserve the
18: original package and audit as immutable evidence. Write a revised package in
19: a new directory; retain existing IDs and keep the revision identity in the
20: sidecar record. Generated Markdown/diagrams are views, never patch authorities.
21: 
22: ## 1. Locate and qualify candidates without reconstructing NL0
23: 
24: Start with existing node statements, direct inputs, definitions and any
25: available index. Locate repeated subarguments using their mathematical role,
26: objects, formulas or operation names; then inspect the actual candidate spans
27: and the local context they need. Do not commission a new proof or a full prose
28: summary for every node as a discovery method. Text similarity is only a lead.
29: 
30: For each proposed lemma record:
31: 
32: - The complete mathematical statement, all parameters/conditions and proposed
33:   direct input IDs, together with exact old graph pointers or paragraph spans.
34: - The existing derivation to reuse and every occurrence that will consume it.
35:   The derivation must actually supply the proposed statement; a summary label
36:   or a theorem believed true from memory is insufficient.
37: - Identify the baseline revision/old paragraph IDs separately from the current
38:   new producer. A new N's origin label must state the historical/current
39:   distinction; a bare old R number is ambiguous after consumer editing.
40: - The expected avoided repeated work. An occurrence count is not measured
41:   formalization cost and does not by itself establish a speed benefit.
42: - The scope at each occurrence, including bound variables, temporary
43:   assumptions, definition guards and local facts established before the span.
44: 
45: Prefer a statement already justified at the cuts. Do not generalize its domain,
46: change representations, weaken conditions or introduce new mathematics merely
47: to make more occurrences match. If the proposed derivation needs an earlier
48: local calculation, include that calculation with its justified inputs. Never
49: declare an unexported local fact to be an available graph input.
50: 
51: Temporary assumptions stay closed in an implication or other complete
52: proposition; they cannot become H roots. An extraction that moves a witness,
53: choice, definition or binder across a scope boundary needs an explicit account
54: of the values and properties used afterwards. If that account cannot be made
55: locally and clearly, leave the original argument in place.
56: 
57: ## 2. Write the patch boundary before editing
58: 
59: Prepare an edit allowlist for one candidate or one coherent batch:
60: 
61: | Part | Allowed edit |
62: | --- | --- |
63: | New shared theorem | One fresh N and its R producer, with a complete statement and derivation from existing permitted inputs. |
64: | Actual consumers | Replace only the located repeated proof spans by a complete application; adjust direct inputs, citations and application accounting accordingly. |
65: | Necessary local bookkeeping | Update the directly affected binder/reference accounting and generated views. Record every such edit explicitly. |
66: | Everything else | Preserve the existing record content; do not reorder or renumber it as a cleanup. |
67: 
68: Keep the entire frozen specification unchanged: target P, original H, parameter
69: domains, global definitions/notation, logic, pins and E/M source inventories and
70: statements. Preserve all existing N/P statements and every unmodified argument
71: span. New sources, changed hypotheses, new global definitions, removed existing
72: nodes, or a changed old output are outside this fast factoring operation.
73: 
74: Copy an existing derivation rather than writing a new proof route. The new
75: producer may use only its declared inputs, global definitions and legitimate
76: local derivations. It cannot depend on a consumer output or its descendants.
77: Do not split each consumer into additional source nodes around the shared fact.
78: 
79: Each consumer application must state the parameter substitution, which inputs
80: or local proved facts discharge each condition, and the exact conclusion used.
81: Remove a former direct input only if the remaining argument no longer uses it;
82: retain it when it still has a direct role. A shared theorem is never ambient.
83: 
84: If an edit escapes the allowlist, return that candidate to the shortlist or
85: leave it unextracted. A source defect goes through the existing gap procedure;
86: do not turn a reuse optimization into a repair or a new research route.
87: 
88: ## 3. Check structural preservation globally, reasoning locally
89: 
90: Compare canonical JSON records by stable IDs, not only rendered text or changed
91: line numbers. Record before/after hashes and the actual changed fields/spans.
92: Reject any unexplained diff. Check these global mechanical invariants:
93: 
94: - The frozen specification and protected records are unchanged.
95: - All IDs/references resolve; definitions and guards remain available; there
96:   is no cycle or unsupported initial node; every N/P still has one producer.
97: - Every retained node remains in P's dependency closure. Reject the candidate
98:   if it would require deleting or reorganizing unrelated nodes to restore this.
99: - All consumers declare their actual inputs and remain self-contained. Only
100:   the explicit allowlisted nodes/fields have changed.
101: 
102: Run the existing `../scripts/nl0.py check` on the revised graph and specification.
103: Rechecking graph metadata across the package is allowed and inexpensive relative
104: to rereading every mathematical proof. It does not require a new LLM proof of
105: every node, and it does not establish the semantics of a substitution.
106: 
107: Distinguish **review impact** from **dependency status**. The new producer and
108: edited application boundaries need new mathematical review. An unchanged
109: downstream proof whose input statements and conventions are unchanged need not
110: be reconstructed merely because its ancestors have a new producer. Its final
111: acceptance nevertheless depends on the replacement producer being accepted.
112: Until that happens, affected descendants are pending, not newly accepted.
113: 
114: ## 4. Incremental Audit A: review the new proof and the substitution cuts
115: 
116: This is an incremental review procedure under Audit A's mathematical
117: obligations, not permission to weaken source verification or invent a fresh
118: packet replay. The version-bound receipt limitation below is part of the rule.
119: 
120: First inspect the baseline audit and its evidence bindings. Reuse a judgment
121: only for the exact previously reviewed content, context and evidence. Carry
122: FAIL, UNVERIFIED, inaccessible sources and disclosure limits forward. A source
123: file hash proves byte identity, not that an auditor ever inspected the theorem.
124: An unaudited baseline cannot acquire whole-proof acceptance through extraction.
125: 
126: Review the **new N/R in full**: complete statement, exact inputs, argument,
127: dependency accounting, scopes, guards and E/M applications, and the normal
128: fresh packet-only replay requirement. The extracted proof may be copied, but
129: its new closed interface and context must actually be checked.
130: 
131: For **each changed consumer**, review a substitution cut rather than rewriting
132: or replaying its entire old proof by default:
133: 
134: 1. Compare the old derived conclusion at the cut with the instantiated shared
135:    result, including all conditions, quantifiers and semantic conventions.
136: 2. Check that every condition of the shared theorem follows from that consumer's
137:    declared inputs or explicit in-scope local derivations, without extra facts.
138: 3. Check the interface to the untouched continuation: every subsequently used
139:    proposition, object, value and scope remains available with the same meaning.
140:    Equal output text alone cannot establish preservation of a selected witness.
141: 4. Verify the changed direct-input/citation/application accounting. Reuse source
142:    identity evidence only when unchanged; check every new source application.
143: 5. Bind the untouched remainder to its old reviewed bytes and old review
144:    evidence. Record exactly which old checks are inherited and which new checks
145:    cover the patch. Do not relabel this comparison as a new fresh whole-R replay.
146: 
147: If those boundaries do not justify inheritance, mark that candidate
148: `DEFERRED_NOT_LOCAL` and keep the baseline argument. Do not automatically expand
149: to a full-case audit. A separately requested broader review may inspect the
150: specific unresolved node, but is not part of this fast extraction.
151: 
152: Unchanged target/source/definition reviews and proof regions need no new
153: mathematical re-review when their audited content, applicable context and
154: evidence are unchanged. Do not reopen source searches solely because a global
155: graph hash changed. Changes or failures in their evidence invalidate reuse.
156: 
157: The result is a chain: baseline audit + exact revision + actual new reviews.
158: It is not a copied PASS with an updated graph hash. Record actual reviewer
159: exposure; old-review access is appropriate for delta review and cannot be called
160: an independent fresh packet-only review. This procedure authorizes no additional
161: agent or external-service dispatch.
162: 
163: ## 5. Seal or leave the candidate unextracted
164: 
165: Seal only after the allowlist/diff and graph checks pass and the scoped
166: mathematical review is complete. Keep original and revised manifests, patch,
167: location map, old/new evidence, pending findings and measured preparation cost.
168: Stage all candidate edits transactionally; a failed candidate must not replace
169: the accepted baseline. Do not launch formalization workers for an unaccepted
170: source revision or reuse task packets bound to the old graph.
171: 
172: Then finalize and freeze typed interfaces, shared Lean ports and local plans;
173: only afterwards generate worker packets. Shared Lean interface discovery may
174: use this preparation pass, but must not silently mutate the sealed NL0 later.
175: No extraction is a valid outcome; do not manufacture shared lemmas to satisfy
176: the workflow. The work is bounded by the chosen proof regions and patch size,
177: not a universal minute count. Longer time alone is not a mathematical gap.
178: 
179: ## Executable acceptance and review responsibilities
180: 
181: The unchanged parent checker still binds ordinary audit v3 to the complete
182: graph. `scripts/source_preparation.py` adds a separate incremental record;
183: it never copies old PASS fields into a forged fresh whole-graph audit.
184: Audit B and `workflow.py` both revalidate that record and all underlying evidence.
185: See [commands and the patch contract](integrated-workflow.md).
186: 
187: The initial executable scope is current-v2 source and nonoverlapping consumer
188: paragraph substitutions. Old proposition records/specification, unlisted R
189: records, untouched paragraphs and local fact/assumption lifetimes are protected.
190: Consumer source-application changes can remove obsolete uses, not introduce new
191: external uses. A broader refactor is deferred rather than widening this operation.
192: Multiple proposed edits to one consumer must first be merged into one coherent
193: candidate or left unextracted. Legacy test copies remain development evidence.
194: 
195: Separate three responsibilities:
196: 
197: - A producer reviewer sees only the complete new per-R packet and audits its
198:   conditional mathematics under ordinary Audit A, including actual fresh replay.
199:   Do not ask that packet to establish whole-graph acceptance or old-copy provenance.
200: - A substitution reviewer sees paired before/after consumers, the proposed shared
201:   statement, original derivations and explicit cut contract. `old_derivation`
202:   names THIS consumer's replaced proof; `producer_source_derivation` names the
203:   one original proof used to export the shared lemma. Its supplier may be a
204:   different consumer with a different final goal. Compare the common intermediate
205:   conclusion, not equality of those final goals. Check existing-proof
206:   factoring, each condition, exact supplied conclusion, continuation and accounting.
207:   This is delta review with baseline access, not fresh whole-consumer replay.
208: - Python checks canonical fanout, edit scope, graph validity, immutable evidence,
209:   the exact coverage partition and inherited acceptance/qualifications. It does
210:   not judge natural-language mathematics or authenticate a dishonest reviewer.
211: 
212: Internal N applications are direct inputs, paragraph citations and explicit prose;
213: the parent's `applications` source records remain E/M-only. Do not invent an N
214: source-application record to satisfy a reviewer. A prose citation without a real
215: substitution is not successful factoring. Derivation labels and fanout guesses
216: from a model are leads, not canonical graph facts.
217: 
218: Each cut review binds the exact supplied packet hash. Retain the binding from
219: the generated template and verify it during acceptance. Reusing an actual old
220: review after a record-only change requires identical canonical mathematics and
221: byte-identical actual reviewed packets; preserve its verdicts, notes, evidence
222: and original cost, and disclose that no new mathematical review occurred.
223: 
224: `INCREMENTAL-AUDIT-A-PASSED` requires a passing current baseline plus all actual
225: new producer/cut reviews. Missing/failed baseline checks remain inherited and
226: yield development-only local review. Every later consumer acceptance still
227: depends on the new producer; unchanged input statements and context permit
228: inheriting the old conditional argument without rereading it mathematically.
229: No fixed completion-time threshold makes a candidate worthwhile or incorrect.

value.full_target:
Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
value.conclusion: dim_H(F)=D+1, where F=E×[0,1] has the Euclidean product metric and D=dim_H(E); equivalently dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1 in ℝ^{n+1}.

parameters.type: natural number (the nonnegative integer ambient dimension)
subset of the Euclidean space ℝ^n

hypotheses.origin: problem.md:21; the nonnegative integer is represented by a natural number, and its explicit range condition is retained.
problem.md:16-23; the disclosed user-approved nonemptiness assumption.

hypotheses.statement: E is compact in the Euclidean topology of ℝ^n.

definitions.type: family of Euclidean metric spaces indexed by natural numbers, together with their coordinate notation
definitions.definition: For each natural k, V(k)=ℝ^k, the functions from {0,...,k-1} to ℝ, with distance d(x,y)=(Σ_{j=0}^{k-1}(x_j-y_j)^2)^(1/2) and its metric topology and Borel measurable structure. V(0) consists of the single empty tuple. ℝ has its usual absolute-value distance. V(k)×ℝ always means the metric with squared distance d(x,y)^2+|t-u|^2, not the max-product metric. Concatenation (x,t)↦(x_0,...,x_{k-1},t) specifies the identification with V(k+1).

definitions.type: extended nonnegative diameter of a subset of a metric or extended metric space
definitions.definition: For an extended metric space X and A⊆X, diam(A)=sup{edist(x,y):x∈A,y∈A} in [0,∞], with supremum of the empty set equal to 0. On a metric space edist is ordinary distance viewed in [0,∞]. This is the native Metric.ediam. When diam(A) is bounded by a finite scale we identify it with its finite nonnegative real value. In particular empty sets and singletons have diameter zero.

definitions.type: positive-exponent unnormalized Hausdorff contents and measure, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero.

binders.type: countable family of subsets of that Euclidean space

definitions.type: native Hausdorff measures on Borel extended metric spaces, indexed by real exponents
definitions.definition: μH[d] on a Borel extended metric space X denotes MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d, defined natively as Measure.mkMetric(r↦r^d), the metric outer-measure construction with diameter gauge r^d followed by its Borel measure. The metric outer construction is the supremum over positive extended scales r of the infimum of Σ_i (sup_{h:U_i≠∅} diam(U_i)^d) over sequences U:ℕ→Set X covering the set and satisfying diam(U_i)≤r. Empty summands are zero, including at exponent zero. Native ENNReal real powers are used. The value formula for the resulting measure on arbitrary subsets is established by the registered native theorem; its identification with H for positive exponents is proved below.

binders.type: extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of a metric space, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For a subset A of a metric space with its Borel structure, dim_H(A)=sup{u:u∈[0,∞) is finite and μH[u](A)=∞}, with supremum of the empty set zero. The metric space may be borelized when no measurable structure was specified. This is the native dimH definition. Thus dim_H(∅)=0 by this convention. In this task it is applied to Euclidean subsets and the Euclidean product metric of V(n)×ℝ.

definitions.type: subset of V(n)×ℝ with the Euclidean product metric
definitions.definition: F=E×I={(x,t):x∈E,t∈I}, using the squared-distance product metric specified in V. Its Euclidean identification is the concatenation map to V(n+1).
D=dim_H(E). When finiteness is proved, finite dimensions are also viewed as nonnegative real numbers through the canonical inclusion ℝ≥0→[0,∞].

definitions.type: predicate on subsets of metric spaces
definitions.definition: Compact(A) means that every family of open sets whose union contains A has a finite subfamily whose union contains A. The word compact has this finite-open-subcover meaning throughout.

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line, also evaluated as outer measure on arbitrary sets
definitions.definition: λ is the native MeasureTheory.volume on ℝ, equivalently the Lebesgue measure whose outer measure is the infimum of sums of lengths of countable open-interval covers. As for any measure, λ is monotone, has λ(∅)=0, and is countably additive on disjoint measurable sets. These measure axioms are part of the measure structure, not any assertion of measurability of the arbitrary covering sets in this proof.

definitions.type: nonnegative Lebesgue integral for an arbitrary measure on a measurable space
definitions.definition: For a measurable space X, a measure ν on it, and f:X→[0,∞], LInt(ν,f)=∫⁻ f dν is the supremum of the simple-function integrals Σ_a a ν(g^{-1}{a}) over nonnegative measurable finite-range simple functions g≤f, with 0·∞=0. This is the native MeasureTheory.lintegral. For measurable f the value may be ∞; no finite-integrability premise is implicit.

binders.type: nonnegative measurable finite-range map on X

definitions.type: indicator operation for nonnegative functions on a set
definitions.definition: For B⊆X and c∈[0,∞], ind(B,c)(t)=c if t∈B and 0 otherwise. It denotes native Set.indicator B (fun _=>c). Thus c·1_B is an alternative notation for ind(B,c).

1: # Local NL0 extraction and incremental-review record
2: 
3: Use [the procedure](../references/source-refactoring.md) and
4: [executable guide](../references/integrated-workflow.md). This worksheet is not
5: itself an acceptance record; the adapter validates the actual JSON reviews.
6: All review fields begin UNVERIFIED and can
7: change only after actual inspection. Keep the baseline files immutable.
8: 
9: ## Baseline and scope
10: 
11: - Baseline canonical graph/spec paths and SHA256:
12: - Baseline Audit A path/SHA256, exact scope, actual status and reviewer disclosure:
13: - Baseline evidence verified; outstanding FAIL/UNVERIFIED items:
14: - Revised package directory and revision identity:
15: - Operation: translation-preparation proof factoring, not NL0 reconstruction.
16: - Protected original target/H/D/E/M/logic/pins and existing N/P statements:
17: - Candidate IDs and proposed edit allowlist:
18: - Mathematical author, delta reviewer and actual prior exposure:
19: 
20: ## One record per candidate
21: 
22: - Candidate ID:
23: - Existing exported N usable instead of new extraction? Explain:
24: - Repeated occurrences: exact old R IDs and JSON pointers/paragraph spans:
25: - Avoided repeated work expected; basis and unmeasured assumptions:
26: - Proposed new N/R IDs:
27: - Full statement with all binders, domains and conditions:
28: - Direct inputs and their roles:
29: - Existing derivation to copy, its source spans and required local context:
30: - Any temporary assumption, witness, choice, definition guard or escaping local:
31: - Why this is an existing derivation, without stronger/generalized mathematics:
32: - Eligibility judgment and actual evidence: UNVERIFIED
33: - Candidate outcome: UNVERIFIED / STAGED / DEFERRED_NOT_LOCAL / REJECTED
34: 
35: ## Patch manifest
36: 
37: | Stable ID / JSON pointer | Before hash / exact span | After hash / exact span | Permitted edit and reason |
38: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
39: 
40: - New producer proof and its mapping to old derivation spans:
41: - Every changed consumer input/citation/application record:
42: - All other mathematical records/spans preserved:
43: - Global graph/spec check command, actual output and artifact hashes:
44: - Cycle/reachability/definition-guard/producer checks:
45: - New source package hashes and actual diff artifact:
46: - Unexplained changes: UNVERIFIED
47: 
48: ## New producer review
49: 
50: Apply the ordinary Audit A obligations to the full new N/R. Record actual
51: source applications and the fresh packet-only replay separately.
52: 
53: - Complete statement, objects and dependency closure: UNVERIFIED
54: - Inputs, argument, accounting and exact output: UNVERIFIED
55: - Scope, guards and E/M applicability: UNVERIFIED
56: - Fresh replay carrier/input boundary, packet hash and evidence: UNVERIFIED
57: - Review verdict and located evidence: UNVERIFIED
58: - Scope: producer packet only; whole-graph acceptance and comparison to the old
59:   derivation belong to the separate substitution/evidence checks.
60: 
61: ## One substitution review per consumer
62: 
63: - Consumer R ID and exact replaced span:
64: - This consumer's old derivation and the separate supplier derivation for the
65:   shared producer; compare intermediate conclusions, not consumer final goals:
66: - Exact reviewed cut packet SHA256; inherited evidence and actual exposure:
67: - Old conclusion at the cut, with binders/conditions/conventions:
68: - Shared theorem instantiation and exact supplied conclusion:
69: - Evidence discharging every application condition:
70: - Facts/objects/values/scopes needed by the unchanged continuation:
71: - Evidence that these remain available and unchanged:
72: - Old source/application accounting and its exact replacement:
73: - Unchanged region hashes and precise baseline judgments inherited:
74: - New judgments covering the changed boundary, with located evidence:
75: - Exposure: delta review with baseline access, not a fresh whole-R replay.
76: - Boundary review verdict: UNVERIFIED
77: - Review the actual source format: N calls use direct inputs/prose, while
78:   `applications` records belong only to E/M; do not require invalid N records.
79: - The shared application replaces the selected derivation rather than merely
80:   adding an annotation; actual before/after evidence: UNVERIFIED
81: - If not local, defer the candidate instead of expanding to whole-case review:
82: 
83: ## Coverage and disposition
84: 
85: - Baseline + new reviews cover each revised proof region; coverage evidence:
86: - Inherited unresolved items and currently blocked descendants:
87: - Actual discovery/edit/check/review elapsed time and any model/tool faults:
88: - Record status: UNVERIFIED / DELTA-REVIEW-PASSED / DEFERRED_NOT_LOCAL / REJECTED
89: - Accepted source revision, or baseline retained; exact reason:
90: - Executable acceptance: source_preparation.py check result and
91:   source-acceptance.json; baseline and all new evidence revalidated by Audit B.
92: - Actual inherited baseline qualifications and reviewer exposure:
93: - Pending work before production acceptance and worker-packet generation:
94: 
95: ## Boundary example
96: 
97: Suppose old R010 and R020 each explicitly derive L(x) from A and B, then use it
98: in different continuations. Copy one complete derivation into a new producer
99: of `for every x in the stated domain, A(x) and B(x) imply L(x)`. At each actual
100: occurrence, keep the same x, discharge A(x)/B(x), and replace only that proof
101: span by this application. Review the new closed statement and each cut.
102: 
103: Do not replace a span that also selected a witness w used later by a theorem
104: merely asserting `there exists w`: that may lose the required value/scope.
105: Defer the extraction unless the exact continuation interface can be preserved.
106: These examples explain the review method; they are not executed controls or
107: evidence that a model correctly follows it.

artifact.reason: Inventory marks every consumer R001–R009 as having accepted background notes, so none is eligible for the current narrow delta route; an extraction cannot have two eligible consumers. The equal-interval covering argument in R004/S001 and R008/S001 is a genuine repeated derivation, but both consumers must remain unchanged. N001, N002 and N005 already export the common Hausdorff facts, compact-set bounds and interval-enclosure facts and should not be duplicated. Additional producer/cut review would therefore yield no admissible replacement or demonstrated savings. Retain the accepted NL0 unchanged.
